title: Reconstruction from components
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product space. At every outcome $x$, the sum of all its components, over all coordinate subsets $S$, equals $f(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with positive coordinate weights summing to one
$f$ is real-valued on the product space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Its orthogonal components satisfy $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}f_S(x)=f(x)$ for every $x\in\Omega$.
